subject: English
stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to the highlighted word: The general ordered his troops to halt immediately.
solution: 'Halt' means to stop; its opposite is to continue or proceed. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to the highlighted word: Despite his initial reluctance, he finally acquiesced to their demands.
solution: 'Acquiesced' means agreed or accepted reluctantly; its opposite is to reject. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Their new colour scheme is \(\underline{\text{hideous}}\).
solution: 'Hideous' means extremely ugly or repulsive; its opposite is 'Attractive'. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to the highlighted word: After years of hard work, he finally found atonement by proving his innocence.
solution: 'Atonement' means making amends or salvation; its opposite is condemnation. Salvation is a synonym, so it is not the answer. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to the highlighted word: The two neighbours were involved in a long feud over their property boundary.
solution: 'Feud' means a prolonged bitter quarrel; its opposite is harmony. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to the highlighted word: Constant delays can vitiate the effectiveness of the entire project.
solution: 'Vitiate' means to spoil, impair or destroy the effectiveness of something; annihilate (to destroy) is the closest. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to the highlighted word: As the sun rose, we stood quietly to behold the breathtaking view.
solution: 'Behold' means to look at or observe; the closest word is look. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to the highlighted word: The king entered the hall wearing a velvet robe embroidered with gold.
solution: A 'robe' is a long loose outer garment, closest in meaning to a cloak. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to the highlighted word: She carefully packed her trousseau before leaving for her new home after the wedding.
optB: Single leg side of a trouser
optC: A large cabinet full of expensive clothes
optD: The clothes, linen, and other belongings collected by a bride for her marriage
solution: 'Trousseau' is the clothes, linen and other belongings a bride collects for her marriage. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: Choose the word CLOSEST in meaning to the highlighted word: The warrior's prowess in battle made him legendary across the kingdom.
solution: 'Prowess' means outstanding skill or expertise, i.e. exceptional mastery. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: Spot the part containing the error: It is be said that in 2019 the (a) / Indian Stock Market will fall (b) / drastically and we can expect that fall very soon. (c) / no error (d)
optA: It is be said that in 2019 the
optC: drastically and we can expect that fall very soon.

subject: English
stem: Spot the part containing the error: What is the function (a) / of the kidney (b) / in the body? (c) / no error (d)
solution: The sentence is grammatically correct throughout. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: Spot the part containing the error: He likes to put (a) / all the garbage (b) / into a black small bag. (c) / no error (d)
solution: Adjective order is wrong; size precedes colour, so it should be 'small black bag'. The error is in part (c). Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: Spot the part containing the error: My father did never have (a) / an opportunity to (b) / go to a University. (c) / no error (d)
solution: 'Did never have' is incorrect; it should be 'never had'. The error is in part (a). Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Spot the part containing the error: Whom did (a) / you give (b) / the packets to? (c) / no error (d)
solution: 'Whom' is correctly used as the object and the sentence is grammatical. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: Spot the part containing the error: He would not have accepted the offer (a) / even if he would have been (b) / in a better financial situation. (c) / no error (d)
optA: He would not have accepted the offer
optB: even if he would have been
solution: In a third-conditional 'if' clause 'would have been' is wrong; it should be 'had been'. The error is in part (b). Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Spot the part containing the error: The minister, as well as his key advisors, (a) / have approved the draft (b) / which is now being sent to the cabinet for final approval. (c) / no error (d)
optA: The minister, as well as his key advisors,
optC: which is now being sent to the cabinet for final approval.
solution: The subject is the singular 'minister' ('as well as' does not change number), so the verb should be 'has approved'. The error is in part (b). Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Spot the part containing the error: The committee appreciated him submitting the report (a) / ahead of schedule but criticized (b) / its lack of substantive data. (c) / no error (d)
optA: The committee appreciated him submitting the report
solution: A gerund takes the possessive, so it should be 'his submitting', not 'him submitting'. The error is in part (a). Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Spot the part containing the error: Had the authorities been more vigilant, (a) / the conspiracy would have been uncovered (b) / and many lives could have been saved. (c) / no error (d)
optA: Had the authorities been more vigilant,
optB: the conspiracy would have been uncovered
optC: and many lives could have been saved.
solution: The inverted third-conditional structure and the following clauses are all grammatically correct. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: Spot the part containing the error: He was angry at me (a) / because I had gone to the party (b) / without telling him. (c) / no error (d)
optB: because I had gone to the party
solution: When directed at a person the correct collocation is ‘angry with’, so ‘angry at me’ should be ‘angry with me’. The error is in part (a).

optB: Peak means top, and Peek means look quickly.

subject: English
stem: Arrange P, Q, R, S between S1 and S6. S1: The current debate on intellectual property rights (IPRs) raises a number of important issues concerning the strategy and policies for building a more dynamic national agricultural research system. S6: The argument was that incentives are necessary to stimulate innovations, and that this calls for a system of patents which gives innovators the sole right to use. P: TRIPs, for the first time, seeks to bring innovations in agricultural technology under a new worldwide IPR regime. Q: The agribusiness MNCs (along with pharmaceutical companies) played a leading part in lobbying for such a regime during the Uruguay Round negotiations. R: With the relative roles of public and private sectors, and the role of agribusiness multinational corporations (MNCs). S: This debate has been stimulated by the international agreement on Trade Related Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPs), negotiated as part of the Uruguay Round.
solution: R completes S1's list of issues, S introduces TRIPs, P explains what TRIPs seeks to do, and Q names the MNCs that lobbied for it, leading to S6. Order RSPQ. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: Arrange P, Q, R, S between S1 and S6. S1: In this genealogy, some pure lines of descent follow their logic to the inevitable point of extinction, others engage in cross-fertilization, and yet others undergo mutation to maintain their energy. S6: Uncharitable as it may sound, the history of Indian abstractionism records a series of attempts to avoid the risks of abstraction. P: It is equally possible to enumerate the troughs where the two principles do not come together, thus arriving at a very different account. Q: However, this genealogical survey demonstrates the wave at its crests at points. R: Ideas sensuously ordained rather than fabricated programmatically to a concept. S: Those points where the metaphysical and the painterly have been fused in images of abiding potency.
solution: Q introduces the crests, S defines those points where metaphysical and painterly fuse, R elaborates the nature of those ideas, and P offers the contrasting troughs. Order QSRP. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Arrange P, Q, R, S between S1 and S6. S1: The narrator of Midnight's Children describes it as a kind of collective fantasy. S6: One could argue that nation-states are a kind of collective fantasy. P: I suppose what he, or I, through him was trying to say, was that there never had been a political entity called India until 1947. Q: It was an invention of the nationalist movement. And a very successful invention. R: So it struck me that what was coming into being, this idea of a nation-state, was an invention. S: The thing that became independent had never previously existed, except that there had been an area, a zone called India.
solution: P states there was no political entity called India until 1947, S adds that what became independent had never existed, R concludes the nation-state was an invention, and Q calls it a successful invention of the nationalist movement. Order PSRQ. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Arrange P, Q, R, S between S1 and S6. S1: Not content with shaking up the multi-billion-dollar market for computer memory, some researchers have even more ambitious plans for magnetic computing. S6: Dr. Cowburn and Dr. Welland have demonstrated how a logic gate could work in such a scheme. P: Outlined research that could form the basis of a magnetic microprocessor, a chip capable of manipulating (rather than merely storing) information magnetically. Q: In a paper published last month in Science, Russell Cowburn and Mark Welland of Cambridge University. R: In place of conducting wires, a magnetic processor would have rows of magnetic dots, each of which could be polarised in one of two directions. S: Individual bits of information would travel down the rows as magnetic pulses, changing the orientation of the dots as they went.
solution: Q names the researchers, P completes the sentence by outlining their research, R describes the magnetic dots replacing wires, and S explains how bits travel down the rows. Order QPRS. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Arrange P, Q, R, S between S1 and S6. S1: From ancient times, men have believed that, under certain peculiar circumstances, life could arise spontaneously. S6: In association with Buffon, the Irish Jesuit priest John Needham declared that he could bring about at will the creation of living microbes. P: This belief was held by Aristotle, Newton and Descartes, among many others, and apparently the great William Harvey too. Q: The weight of centuries gradually disintegrated men's beliefs in the spontaneous origin of maggots and mice. R: From the ooze of rivers could come eels and from the entrails of dead bulls, bees; worms from mud, and maggots from dead meat. S: But the doctrine of spontaneous generation clung tenaciously to the question of bacterial origin.
solution: P names the believers (Aristotle, Newton, Descartes), R gives concrete examples of the belief (eels, bees, worms, maggots), Q notes that the weight of centuries eroded the belief in the spontaneous origin of maggots and mice, and S adds that the doctrine still clung to bacterial origin, leading to S6. Order PRQS. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: What can be inferred from the passage about the primary tension in India’s energy policy?
optA: Balancing economic growth with energy imports
optB: Reconciling environmental commitments with energy security and socio-economic priorities
optC: Prioritizing coal-based energy over renewable sources
optD: Eliminating fossil fuel subsidies to promote green hydrogen
solution: The passage frames India’s core dilemma as balancing its Paris-Agreement environmental commitments against energy security and socio-economic concerns (e.g. coal-region livelihoods). Option B captures this tri-fold tension.
context: India’s quest for energy security in the 21st century is a complex interplay of economic ambition, environmental imperatives, and geopolitical strategy. With rising energy demands driven by industrialization and urbanization, India relies heavily on fossil fuels, importing over 80% of its crude oil and significant natural gas. This dependency exposes the economy to global price volatility and geopolitical tensions, particularly in the Middle East. Concurrently, India’s commitment to the Paris Agreement necessitates a rapid transition to renewable energy, with ambitious targets of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030. However, scaling renewables faces hurdles like land acquisition, intermittency issues, and inadequate grid infrastructure. The push for green energy intersects with socio-economic challenges. Coal-dependent regions, such as Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh, face potential economic disruption due to the shift away from coal, necessitating a just transition framework to protect livelihoods. Meanwhile, initiatives like the International Solar Alliance (ISA) position India as a global leader in renewable energy diplomacy, but domestic policy inconsistencies, such as subsidies for fossil fuels, undermine progress. The rise of green hydrogen as a potential game-changer further complicates the energy landscape, demanding significant investment and technological innovation. Geopolitically, India must navigate a multipolar world where energy is a strategic asset. Collaborations with countries like Russia and the US for energy supplies coexist with tensions over technology transfers and sanctions. The challenge lies in balancing energy sovereignty with global cooperation, ensuring that India’s energy transition aligns with its developmental goals without compromising environmental or strategic autonomy.

solution: The passage explicitly cites hurdles such as land acquisition, intermittency and inadequate grid infrastructure. Option B states these structural and logistical constraints.

stem: ____did you know Ravi has a new job?

stem: _______the wind, it was getting stronger, and I was getting colder.
solution: 'Speaking of' transitions to a related topic just mentioned or implied (the wind). Matches option D: Speaking of.

subject: English
stem: _____, what are you doing in my room?
solution: 'Excuse me' is the natural polite interjection used to attract attention or express mild surprise. Matches option B: Excuse me.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Consider the following diagram of a river with sections marked A, B, C, and D (a meandering river bifurcating and reuniting). In which one among the following lettered areas of the diagram would erosion most likely change the shape of the riverbed?
solution: Section B lies on the outer bank of the meander bend, where the swift current erodes and reshapes the riverbed.

subject: Geography
stem: Where is the Mekong Delta located?
solution: The Mekong Delta lies in southern Vietnam, where the Mekong River empties into the South China Sea.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following is known as uplands of delta region?
solution: The uplands within a delta region are locally termed 'Peh'. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: 'Majuli', the river island, is located in which one of the following rivers?
solution: Majuli, the world's largest river island, lies in the Brahmaputra river in Assam.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: Brahmaputra and Indus rivers are antecedent rivers. Which one of the following may be the true definition of an antecedent drainage?
optA: Which follows the initial slope of the Himalaya
optB: Which existed before the Himalayan range came into existence
optC: Which followed the dip of rock beds of the Himalaya
optD: Which followed the strike of rock beds of the Himalaya
solution: An antecedent river existed before the mountain range and kept its original course as the land was uplifted around it.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: A deep valley characterized by steep step-like slopes is known as:
solution: A canyon is a deep, narrow river-cut valley with steep, step-like sides.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following features is the result of both erosion and deposition work of a river?
solution: An oxbow lake forms by both erosion (cutting the meander neck) and deposition (sealing the cut-off ends).

subject: Geography
subtopic: World — Rivers, Canals and Water Bodies
stem: This river originates in the Hindu Kush mountain range and flows into the Hamoun wetlands after covering about 1,100 km. There have been serious conflicts between two neighbouring nations regarding sharing of its water. Identify the river.
solution: The Helmand rises in the Hindu Kush, ends in the Hamoun wetlands, and its waters are contested between Afghanistan and Iran.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem: In India, glacial terraces known as 'Karewas' are found in:
solution: Karewas are lacustrine glacial deposits of the Kashmir (Jhelum) Valley, famed for saffron cultivation.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Basket-of-eggs topography is related to:
solution: Basket-of-eggs topography describes clusters of oval glacial hills called drumlins.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem: If you want to observe moraines, eskers and outwash plains, which one of the following Union Territories would you visit?
solution: These are glacial landforms, found in the glaciated Himalayan Union Territory of Ladakh.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: In the Thar region, shifting sand dunes are locally known as:
solution: In the Thar Desert the shifting/moving sand dunes are locally called Dhrian.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem:
Which of the following statements regarding Barchan is/are correct?
1. It is a crescent-shaped mound of sand deposited by wind blowing constantly from one direction in a desert.
2. The windward side has a gentle slope and the leeward side is steep.
3. The horns of a barchan point in the direction of the wind.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: As printed, all three are true of a barchan — crescent mound from a constant wind, gentle windward and steep leeward slope, and horns pointing downwind (in the direction the wind blows).

subject: Geography

stem: The lowest part of most bolsons is occupied by a landform called playa. Which category of landform formation does it represent?
solution: Playas are flat, dry desert-basin lake beds — characteristic arid landforms.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following is NOT a coastal depositional feature?
solution: A stack is a wave-erosional feature; tombolo, sand bar and spit are depositional.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem:
Which of the following are coastal erosional features?
1. Notch
2. Sea arch
3. Cliff
4. Hook
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: Notch, sea arch and cliff are wave-erosional; a hook is a depositional feature.

optA: Stalactites hang from the ceiling and stalagmites hang from the floor
optB: Stalactites hang from the ceiling and stalagmites rise from the floor
optC: Stalactites rise from the floor and stalagmites hang from the ceiling
solution: Stalactites hang down from a cave ceiling while stalagmites build upward from the cave floor.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Stalactite, stalagmite and pillars are depositional landforms of:
solution: These speleothems form by calcium-carbonate deposition from underground water in limestone caves.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: An upfold in rock is known as:
solution: An arch-shaped upfold of strata is an anticline; a downfold is a syncline.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
subtopic: Earth's Interior, Crust and Plate Tectonics
stem: In which one of the following folds is the axial plane virtually horizontal?
solution: In a recumbent fold the axial plane is overturned to lie nearly horizontal.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: A large body of magmatic material that cools at great depth in the Earth's crust and develops in the form of large domes is known as:
solution: A batholith is a large, deep-seated intrusive mass exposed by erosion as broad domes.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: The formation of 'tors' on small rocky hills is associated with:
solution: Tors form by deep chemical weathering along joints in granite followed by removal of the weathered debris.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following is the lowermost/innermost intrusive igneous body?
solution: The batholith is the largest, deepest intrusive body, forming the base of mountain ranges.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following is NOT an example of a fold mountain?
solution: Mt. Fuji is a volcanic (composite) mountain; the Alps, Andes and Rockies are fold mountains.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List I (Geomorphic Agent)
A. Ground water
B. Running water
C. Glacier
D. Wind
List II (Feature)
1. Plunge pool
2. Horns
3. Playas
4. Lapies
solution: Ground water carves lapies (4), running water forms plunge pools (1), glaciers produce horns (2), and wind creates playas (3): A-4, B-1, C-2, D-3.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: The Defence Investiture Ceremony 2026 witnessed the presentation of Kirti Chakra, Shaurya Chakra and Vir Chakra by the President of India. The President is the:
optB: Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces
solution: Under the Constitution the President of India is the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces. Matches option B.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: The primary objective of the Axiom-4 Mission, in which an Indian astronaut participated, was:
optB: Conducting scientific experiments aboard the International Space Station
solution: Axiom-4 was a private crewed mission to the International Space Station whose goal was to conduct scientific experiments aboard the ISS. Matches option B.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Which of the following groupings is primarily associated with strategic cooperation in the Indo-Pacific region?
solution: The QUAD (India, USA, Japan and Australia) is the grouping focused on strategic cooperation in the Indo-Pacific. Matches option B.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Exercise Sada Tanseeq, seen in recent current affairs, is a joint military exercise between India and:
solution: Exercise Sada Tanseeq is the bilateral joint military exercise between India and Saudi Arabia. Matches option B.

subject: Current Affairs
subtopic: Civilian Awards, Honours and Educational Institutions
stem: The Padma Awards in India are announced every year on the occasion of:
solution: The Padma Awards are announced each year on the eve of Republic Day. Matches option B.

subject: History
stem: Two popular Assemblies of the Vedic period were
solution: The two principal popular assemblies of the Vedic polity were the Sabha and the Samiti. Matches option A.

subject: History
stem: The ritualistic precepts pertaining to the hymns of the Vedas are known as the
solution: The Brahmanas are the prose texts explaining the ritualistic application of the Vedic hymns. Matches option C.

subject: History
stem: Which of the following contains the famous Gayatri Mantra?
solution: The Gayatri Mantra occurs in the third mandala of the Rigveda. Matches option B.

subject: History
stem:
The Rig-Vedic Aryans were a pastoral people is born out by the fact that
I. There are many references to the cow in the Rig-Veda
II. Most of the wars were fought for the sake of cows
III. Gifts made to priests were usually cows
optA: There are many references to the cow in the Rig-Veda
optB: Most of the wars were fought for the sake of cows
optC: Gifts made to priests were usually cows
solution: Cattle-centred references, cattle-raid wars (gavishti) and cattle as gifts all point to a pastoral society. Matches option D.

subject: History
stem: The famous Vedic river which had long ago become extinct and now supposed to be flowing underground in Rajasthan is
solution: The Saraswati is the revered Vedic river now believed to have dried up and flow underground in Rajasthan. Matches option B.

subject: History
stem: The rivers Ganga and Yamuna are mentioned for the first time in:
solution: The Ganga and Yamuna find their earliest mention in the Rigveda (the Nadistuti Sukta). Matches option D.

subject: History
stem: The famous dialogue between Nachiketa and Yama is mentioned in the:
solution: The dialogue between Nachiketa and Yama on death and the soul is recorded in the Kathopanishad. Matches option A.

subject: History
stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the source of Vedic Civilisation:
I. The most important source of Vedic Civilisation is the Vedas.
II. The Vedas are neither any individual religious work nor a collection of a definite number of books compiled at a particular time.
III. It consists of three successive classes of literary creations.
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
solution: All three statements correctly describe the Vedas as the chief source, composed over time as successive classes of literature. Matches option D.

subject: History
stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the age of Vedic Civilisation:
I. Bal Gangadhar Tilak, on astronomical grounds, dated Rig Veda to 6000 B.C. to Harmon Jacobi, Vedic civilization flourished between 4500 B.C. and 2500 B.C. and the Samhitas were composed in the latter half of the period.
II. Famous Sanskritist, Winternitz felt that the Rig Veda was probably composed in the third millennium B.C.
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
solution: Both statements correctly report the datings by Tilak/Jacobi and by Winternitz. Matches option C.

subject: History
stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the Rig Vedic States and its territory:
I. The territory known to Vedic people was divided into a number of states-republican and monarchical.
II. The battle of ten kings, gives names of ten kings who participated in a war against Sudas who was Bharata king of Tritsus family.
III. The ten kings were of the states of Purus, Yadus, Turvasas, Anus and Druhyus along with five others viz Alinas, Pakhtas, Bhalanas, Sibis and Vishanins.
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
solution: All three statements correctly describe the Vedic states and the Dasarajna (battle of ten kings) against Sudas. Matches option D.

subject: History
stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the four Vedas
I. Rig-Veda is a collection of hymns
II. Samveda is a collection of songs mostly taken from Rig Veda
III. Atharvaveda is a collection of sacrificial formulae
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
solution: I and II are correct; III is wrong because sacrificial formulae belong to the Yajurveda while the Atharvaveda is a collection of magical spells and charms. Matches option B.

subject: History
stem: Which of the correct ascending order of Political structure of Rig Vedic India?
solution: The ascending Vedic political units run Kula (family), Grama (village), Vis (clan), Jana (tribe) and Rashtra (kingdom). Matches option B.

subject: History
stem:
Consider the following statement regarding the Brahamana text of Vedic Civilisation:
I. The Brahamanas are the collection of ancient Vedic texts with commentaries on the hymns of the four Vedas.
II. The Brahamanas contain details about the meaning of Vedic hymns, their applications, stories of their origins, etc.
III. Chandogya Brahmana, one of the oldest Brahmana, includes eight suktas (hymns) for the ceremony of marriage and rituals at the birth of a child.
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
solution: All three statements correctly describe the Brahmanas and the marriage/birth hymns of the Chandogya (Mantra) Brahmana. Matches option D.

subject: History
stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the "Vedas":
I. The word 'Veda' signifies knowledge and they are actually providing humans with knowledge to conduct their life on Earth.
II. The Vedas were initially handed down orally by generations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Both statements are correct: Veda means knowledge and the texts were transmitted orally across generations before being written. Matches option C.

subject: History
stem: Which of the following text is contemporary to Vedas?
solution: The Zend Avesta, the Iranian scripture closely related in language and content to the Rigveda, is contemporary to the Vedas. Matches option B.

subject: History
stem: The ninth mandala of the Rigveda samhita is devoted wholly to:
optC: Gods related to plants and drugs
optD: 'Soma' and the god who is named after the drink
solution: The ninth mandala of the Rigveda is dedicated entirely to Soma Pavamana, the deified sacred drink. Matches option D.

subject: History
stem: Which one of the following stages of the life of man in Aryan Society, in ascending order of age, is correct?
solution: The four ashramas in order of increasing age are Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha and Sanyasa. Matches option C.

subject: History
stem: The Aryans succeeded in their conflicts with the pre-Aryans because:
optA: they used elephants on a large scale
optB: they used chariots driven by horses
optD: they were from an advanced urban culture
solution: The Aryans' advantage lay in their swift horse-drawn chariots. Matches option B.

subject: History
stem: Which one of the following is INCORRECTLY matched?
optA: Yajur Veda- knowledge of the sacrificial formulas
optB: Atharva Veda- knowledge of the magic formulas
optC: Rig Veda- knowledge of the Hymns of Praise
solution: The Sama Veda is the knowledge of melodies and chants, not of science, so this pairing is incorrect. Matches option D.

subject: History
stem: Which of the following is false as per Vedic theory?
optA: The Kshatriyas, or warrior rulers, came from Purusha's arms
optB: The Vaishyas, or the commoners, came from Purusha's thighs
optC: The Brahmans, or priests, came from Purusha's ears
optD: The Shudras, or laborers and servants, came from Purusha's feet
solution: Per the Purusha Sukta the Brahmans emerged from the mouth of Purusha, not the ears, so this statement is false. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: A body freely falling from rest has a velocity \(v\) after it falls through a height \(h\). The distance it has to fall further for its velocity to become double is
solution: For free fall from rest, \(v^{2}=2gh\), so \(v\propto\sqrt{h}\). To double the velocity the total fall must be \(4h\) (since \((2v)^{2}=2g\cdot 4h\)). Having already fallen \(h\), the further distance is \(4h-h=3h\). Matches option (A).

subject: Physics
stem: For the velocity-time graph shown in the figure, the distance covered by the body in the last two seconds of its motion is what fraction of the total distance covered in all the seven seconds? (The velocity rises linearly from \(0\) to \(10\,\text{ms}^{-1}\) between \(t=1\,\text{s}\) and \(t=3\,\text{s}\), stays constant at \(10\,\text{ms}^{-1}\) from \(t=3\,\text{s}\) to \(t=5\,\text{s}\), then falls linearly back to \(0\) between \(t=5\,\text{s}\) and \(t=7\,\text{s}\).)
solution: Distance is the area under the graph. Rising part \(=\tfrac12(2)(10)=10\,\text{m}\), constant part \(=(2)(10)=20\,\text{m}\), falling (last two seconds) \(=\tfrac12(2)(10)=10\,\text{m}\). Total \(=40\,\text{m}\). Fraction in the last two seconds \(=\tfrac{10}{40}=\tfrac14\). Matches option (B).

subject: Physics
stem: A boy is running along a circular track of radius \(7\,\text{m}\). He completes one circle in \(10\) second. The average velocity of the boy is
solution: Average velocity \(=\dfrac{\text{net displacement}}{\text{time}}\). After one complete circle the displacement is zero, so the average velocity is zero. Matches option (C).

subject: Physics
stem: Two bodies in circular paths of radii \(1:2\) take the same time to complete their circles. The ratio of their linear speeds is
solution: Linear speed \(v=\dfrac{2\pi r}{T}\). With equal periods, \(v\propto r\), so the ratio of speeds equals the ratio of radii \(=1:2\). Matches option (A).

subject: Physics
stem: A car travels \(\left(\tfrac{1}{4}\right)^{\text{th}}\) of a circle with radius \(r\). The ratio of the distance to its displacement is
solution: Distance along a quarter circle \(=\tfrac14(2\pi r)=\dfrac{\pi r}{2}\). Displacement is the chord joining two points \(90^{\circ}\) apart \(=\sqrt{r^{2}+r^{2}}=r\sqrt{2}\). Ratio \(=\dfrac{\pi r/2}{r\sqrt{2}}=\dfrac{\pi}{2\sqrt{2}}\), i.e. \(\dfrac{\pi}{2\sqrt{2}}:1\). Matches option (B).

subject: Physics
stem: A number of forces acting on a body changes the velocity of the body. The forces cannot be
solution: A change in velocity means a non-zero net force, so the forces must be unbalanced; they cannot be balanced. Matches option (C).

subject: Physics
stem: When a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun recoils to
solution: The bullet gains forward momentum, so the gun must gain equal and opposite (backward) momentum to keep the total momentum of the isolated system zero. The recoil conserves momentum. Matches option (B).

subject: Physics
stem: If the action and reaction were to act on the same body
optB: The body would not move at all
optC: Both A and B are correct
optD: Neither A nor B is correct
solution: Action and reaction are equal and opposite; acting on the same body they would cancel, giving zero resultant and no motion. Hence both statements are correct. Matches option (C).

subject: Physics
stem: Newton used 'quantity of motion' for
solution: Newton's term 'quantity of motion' refers to momentum (mass times velocity). Matches option (A).

subject: Physics
stem: The type of force that exists between two charged bodies is
solution: Charged bodies also have mass, so both a gravitational force (due to mass) and an electrostatic force (due to charge) act between them, although the electrostatic force is far larger. Matches option (D).

subject: Physics
stem: A ball is thrown up and attains a maximum height of \(19.6\,\text{m}\). Its initial speed was

subject: Physics
stem: The weight of a body is \(120\,\text{N}\) on the earth. If it is taken to the moon, its weight will be about
solution: Acceleration due to gravity on the moon is about \(\tfrac16\) that on earth, so the weight becomes \(\tfrac{120}{6}=20\,\text{N}\). Matches option (C).

subject: Physics
stem: \(1\,\text{N/m}^{2}\) equals
solution: Pressure of one newton per square metre is by definition one pascal: \(1\,\text{N/m}^{2}=1\,\text{Pa}\). Matches option (A).

subject: Physics
stem: Work done
optC: Can be positive, negative or zero
solution: Work \(=Fd\cos\theta\); it is positive when \(\theta<90^{\circ}\), negative when \(\theta>90^{\circ}\), and zero when \(\theta=90^{\circ}\) or the displacement is zero. Matches option (C).

subject: Physics
stem: A body at rest can have
solution: A body at rest has zero speed, velocity and momentum, but it can still possess energy (for example gravitational potential energy). Matches option (D).

subject: Physics
stem: Which one is not the unit of energy?
solution: Kilocalorie, kilowatt-hour and erg are all units of energy, whereas the watt is the unit of power, not energy. Matches option (D).

subject: Physics
stem: A \(1\,\text{kg}\) mass has K.E. of \(1\,\text{J}\) when its speed is
solution: \(\text{K.E.}=\tfrac12 mv^{2}\Rightarrow 1=\tfrac12(1)v^{2}\Rightarrow v^{2}=2\Rightarrow v=\sqrt{2}\approx 1.4\,\text{ms}^{-1}\). Matches option (C).

subject: Physics
subtopic: Sound Behaviours — Reflection, Echo, Reverberation, Beats
stem: For the echo of the last syllable of the speech to be heard, the least distance of the reflector must be (approximately)
solution: For an echo to be heard distinctly the reflected sound must return after the persistence of hearing. Taking the syllable/persistence time \(t\approx0.13\,\text{s}\) and \(v=340\,\text{ms}^{-1}\), the minimum reflector distance is \(d=\tfrac{v\,t}{2}=\tfrac{340\times0.13}{2}\approx22\,\text{m}\). Matches option A.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Wave Equation, Speed, and Frequency Bands
stem: Infrasonic frequency range is
solution: Infrasonic (infrasound) refers to frequencies below the audible range, i.e. below \(20\,\text{Hz}\). Matches option (A).

subject: Physics
subtopic: Foundations — Sound, Perception, and the Ear
stem: The eardrum is a
solution: The eardrum (tympanic membrane) is a thin stretched membrane that vibrates when sound waves strike it. Matches option (C).

subject: Physics
stem: A child walks towards a fixed plane mirror at a speed of \(5\,\text{km h}^{-1}\). The velocity of the image with respect to the mirror is
solution: For a plane mirror the image is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front. As the object approaches at \(5\,\text{km h}^{-1}\), the image approaches the mirror at the same speed but moves in the direction opposite to the object; taking the object's direction as positive, the image velocity relative to the mirror is \(-5\,\text{km h}^{-1}\). (Relative to the object it would be \(10\,\text{km h}^{-1}\).) Matches option (B).

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: The speed of light in vacuum is \(3.0\times10^{8}\,\text{m/s}\). If the refractive index of a transparent liquid is \(\tfrac{4}{3}\), then the speed of light in the liquid is
solution: \(v=\dfrac{c}{n}=\dfrac{3.0\times10^{8}}{4/3}=3.0\times10^{8}\times\dfrac{3}{4}=2.25\times10^{8}\,\text{m/s}\). Matches option (A).

subject: Physics
stem: Focal length of coloured goggles (without number) is
solution: Plain coloured goggles have no lens power (they are flat plates that only filter colour), so their focal length is infinity. Matches option (B).

subject: Physics
stem: The power of a lens whose focal length is \(25\,\text{cm}\) is
solution: Power \(P=\dfrac{1}{f(\text{in metres})}=\dfrac{1}{0.25}=4\,\text{D}\). Matches option (A).

subject: Physics
stem: How many electrons in \(1\,\text{s}\) constitute a current of \(1\,\text{A}\)?
solution: A current of \(1\,\text{A}\) is \(1\,\text{C/s}\); number of electrons \(=\dfrac{1}{1.6\times10^{-19}}=6.25\times10^{18}\). Matches option (A).

subject: Physics
stem: A fuse wire is always connected to the
solution: A fuse is connected in series with the live (phase) wire so that when it blows the appliance is disconnected from the live supply. Matches option (C).

subject: Physics
stem: In electric fittings in a house
optA: the live wire goes through the switch
optB: the neutral wire goes through the switch
optC: the earth wire goes through the switch
optD: no wire goes through the switch
solution: The switch is always placed in the live wire so that, when it is off, the appliance is isolated from the live supply. Matches option (A).

subject: Physics
stem: Three resistances each of \(8\,\Omega\) are connected in a triangle. The resistance between any two terminals will be
solution: Between any two corners one \(8\,\Omega\) arm is in parallel with the other two arms in series \((8+8=16\,\Omega)\): \(\dfrac{8\times16}{8+16}=\dfrac{128}{24}=\dfrac{16}{3}\,\Omega\). Matches option (D).

subject: Physics
stem: In the given circuit, the effective resistance between points A and C will be. (Square with A top-left, D top-right, C bottom-right, B bottom-left; sides A-D, D-C, A-B and B-C each \(R\), and a diagonal A-C \(=2R\).)
solution: Three parallel paths join A and C: the diagonal \(2R\), the route A-D-C \((R+R=2R)\) and the route A-B-C \((R+R=2R)\). Three \(2R\) resistors in parallel give \(\dfrac{2R}{3}\). Matches option (C).

subject: Physics
stem: The resistance of a conductor is reduced to half its initial value. In doing so the heating effect in the conductor will become
solution: At constant applied voltage, heat \(H=\dfrac{V^{2}}{R}t\); halving \(R\) doubles \(H\). Matches option (D).

subject: Physics
stem: Coming of live wire and neutral wire in direct contact causes
solution: Direct contact of the live and neutral wires gives a near-zero-resistance path, so a very large current flows: this is a short circuit. Matches option (A).

subject: Physics
stem: The focal length of the eye lens is controlled by
solution: The ciliary muscles change the curvature (and hence focal length) of the eye lens to focus objects at different distances. Matches option (C).

subject: Physics
stem: Rainbow is formed due to
optA: reflection and dispersion of light through the water droplets
optB: total internal reflection, refraction and dispersion of light through the water droplets
solution: A rainbow forms when sunlight undergoes refraction on entering a water droplet, total internal reflection at its back surface, and dispersion into its component colours. Matches option (B).
reviewNote: Bank row's simple option was 'Dispersion of light'; the printed set is more detailed and the physically complete answer is (B) total internal reflection, refraction and dispersion.

subject: Physics
stem: A convex lens of suitable focal length can correct
solution: Long sightedness (hypermetropia) is corrected by a converging (convex) lens, which brings the image of near objects onto the retina. Matches option (B).

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
stem: Lenz's law
optA: is the same as the right hand palm rule
optB: determines the magnitude of an induced e.m.f.
optC: bears no relation to the law of conservation of energy
optD: is useful in deciding about the direction of an induced e.m.f.
solution: Lenz's law gives the direction of the induced e.m.f./current (it opposes the change in flux) and is a consequence of conservation of energy. Matches option (D).

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
stem: When a bar magnet is broken into two pieces
optA: we will have a single pole on each piece
optB: each piece will have two unlike poles
optC: each piece will have two like poles
solution: Isolated magnetic poles do not exist; each broken piece becomes a complete magnet with its own north and south (two unlike) poles. Matches option (B).

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
stem: Current is induced in a coil by electromagnetic induction when
optA: Only the coil moves in a magnetic field
optB: Only the magnet is moved into a coil
optC: Coil and the magnet move with respect to each other
solution: An e.m.f. is induced whenever there is relative motion (changing flux) between the coil and the magnet, which covers all such cases. Matches option (C).

subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetism and Magnetic Effects of Current
stem: AC is preferred because
solution: AC can be stepped up to high voltage with transformers, greatly reducing \(I^{2}R\) losses, which makes long-distance transmission economical. Matches option (C).

subject: Physics
stem: Which of the following is not an example of a bio-mass energy source?
solution: Wood, gobar-gas (biogas) and coal are all biomass-derived fuels, whereas nuclear energy comes from nuclear fission, not biomass. Matches option (C).

subject: Physics
stem: The source of energy of the sun is
solution: The sun's energy comes from the nuclear fusion of hydrogen nuclei into helium in its core. Matches option (C).

subject: Physics
stem: The number of neutrons in an atom X of atomic number \(Z\) and mass number \(A\) is
solution: Mass number \(A\) = protons \(+\) neutrons \(=Z+N\), so the number of neutrons \(N=A-Z\). Matches option (C).

subject: Physics
stem: Which one of the figures gives the temperature dependence of the density of water correctly?
optA: Density rises to a maximum then falls as temperature increases (dome-shaped curve)
optB: Density increases linearly (straight line rising) with temperature
optC: Density decreases linearly (straight line falling) with temperature
optD: Density stays constant (horizontal line) with temperature
solution: Water shows anomalous expansion: its density increases from \(0^{\circ}\text{C}\) to a maximum at \(4^{\circ}\text{C}\) and then decreases on further heating, giving a rise-then-fall (dome) curve. Matches option (a).
reviewNote: Options are graphs, not text; option text describes each plotted curve. Correct curve keyed by physics (density maximum of water at 4 C). Kept PRIVATE / flawed for OMR.

subject: Physics
stem: Which of the following pairs of physical quantities does not have the same dimensional formula?
solution: Work and torque are both \(\text{ML}^{2}\text{T}^{-2}\); angular momentum and Planck's constant are both \(\text{ML}^{2}\text{T}^{-1}\); impulse and momentum are both \(\text{MLT}^{-1}\). Tension is a force \((\text{MLT}^{-2})\) but surface tension is force per unit length \((\text{MT}^{-2})\), so this pair differs. Matches option (c).

subject: Physics
chapter: Fluid Mechanics and Properties of Matter
stem: Along a streamline
optA: the velocity of a fluid particle remains constant
optB: the velocity of all fluid particles crossing a given position is constant
optC: the velocity of all fluid particles at a given instant is constant
optD: the speed of a fluid particle remains constant
solution: In steady flow the velocity at any fixed point is constant in time, so every fluid particle that crosses a given position on the streamline has the same velocity there. A single particle's own velocity still changes as it moves along the streamline. Matches option (b).

subject: Physics
stem: Assuming the earth to have a constant density, point out which of the following curves shows the variation of acceleration due to gravity from the centre of the earth to points far away from the surface of the earth.
optA: g stays constant inside the earth then decreases outside (flat top, then curved fall after R)
optB: g rises linearly to a peak at R then decreases linearly (triangular)
optC: g rises linearly from zero at the centre to a maximum at the surface R, then decreases as an inverse-square curve outside
solution: Inside a uniform earth \(g\propto r\) (linear rise from zero at the centre to a maximum at the surface \(R\)); outside \(g\propto 1/r^{2}\) (curved decay). The curve that rises linearly to R and then falls off as an inverse-square curve is correct. Matches option (c).
reviewNote: Options are graphs, not text; option text describes each plotted curve. Correct curve keyed by physics (g proportional to r inside, 1/r^2 outside). Kept PRIVATE / flawed for OMR.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Simple Harmonic Motion and General Waves
stem: The acceleration of a particle executing SHM, at its mean position, is
solution: In SHM the acceleration \(a=-\omega^{2}x\). At the mean position \(x=0\), so the acceleration is zero (while the speed is maximum). Matches option (d).

subject: Physics
subtopic: Wave Equation, Speed, and Frequency Bands
stem: The speed of a sound wave in air
solution: Humid air is less dense than dry air (water vapour is lighter than nitrogen and oxygen), so \(v=\sqrt{\gamma P/\rho}\) increases; the speed of sound increases with humidity. It is independent of pressure but increases with temperature. Matches option (c).

subject: Physics
stem: Which of the following figures represents the variation of particle momentum \(p\) with the associated de-Broglie wavelength \(\lambda\)?
optA: p increases linearly with lambda (straight line rising)
optB: p increases with lambda as an upward-curving line
optC: p decreases linearly with lambda (straight line falling)
optD: p decreases with lambda as a rectangular-hyperbola curve (p proportional to 1/lambda)
solution: The de-Broglie relation is \(\lambda=\dfrac{h}{p}\), so \(p=\dfrac{h}{\lambda}\), i.e. \(p\propto\dfrac{1}{\lambda}\): a rectangular hyperbola falling with \(\lambda\). Matches option (d).
reviewNote: Options are graphs, not text; option text describes each plotted curve. Correct curve keyed by physics (p = h/lambda, hyperbola). Kept PRIVATE / flawed for OMR.

subject: Physics
stem: An alternating current can be converted into direct current by a
solution: A rectifier (using diodes) converts alternating current into direct current. Matches option (d).

subject: Physics
stem: Which of the following electromagnetic waves have the longest wavelength?
solution: Among heat (infrared), visible light, radio and ultraviolet waves, radio waves have the longest wavelength. Matches option (c).
